writeup: TIC 334414710 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 18.270473 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 9.94 percent dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal has a high detection significance of 196.3 in the BLS periodogram, and pixel-level difference imaging confirms the eclipse with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 35.6, though the centroid offset of 3.1 arcsec from the target raises a question about whether the signal originates precisely at the expected location. The candidate does not appear in six checked variable-star catalogs. However, an important caveat exists: the alternating eclipse depths show a large statistical deviation (z-score 32.84), suggesting the true orbital period may be double the initially detected value, which is why the corrected period of 18.270473 days is reported here.
